events.subtitle: Hiromi-curated pre-concert for the inaugural MET JAZZ TOKYO festival
events.category: Exceptional Japanese jazz / Festival prelude / Curated ensemble
events.factual_description: Bunkamura presents MET JAZZ TOKYO: DAY 0 on November 29, 2026 at 5:30 PM in Orchard Hall. The event is the pre-concert for the new MET JAZZ TOKYO festival scheduled to launch in May 2027 and is curated by festival ambassador Hiromi. The announced lineup brings together Hiromi, Shun Ishiwaka, May Inoue, Misaki Umei, Riko Sasaki, Takashi Sugawa, Riku Takahashi, Kaito Nakamura, Tomoaki Baba and Shutaro Matsui as a concentrated snapshot of the current Japanese jazz scene.

enrichment.note: The exact Bunkamura event page is verified. Its MY Bunkamura presale ran August 1-9, 2026, while the page currently states that the general on-sale date is undecided; no currently actionable exact public purchase destination is committed yet.

provenance.note: Date, start time, venue, festival-prelude framing, Hiromi curation, full announced lineup and ticket-sale status were verified on Bunkamura's exact event page. MET JAZZ TOKYO's official site independently verifies the new festival, Hiromi as ambassador, Makoto Ozone and Shun Ishiwaka as co-ambassadors, and its May 2027 launch.

en.why_it_matters: This clears the S bar because it is not simply a festival sampler: it is the one-night public prologue to a new Tokyo jazz institution, curated by Hiromi, with a deliberately intergenerational concentration of players who embody the contemporary Japanese scene. Ishiwaka, Inoue, Baba, Matsui, Umei and the rest give the night a strong instrumental and improvisational identity, while the Day 0 framing makes it a cultural marker for where Tokyo jazz wants to go next.
en.trip_verdict: S within Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Protect the night and cross Tokyo for it; it is especially valuable as a concentrated snapshot of modern Japanese jazz and as the ceremonial beginning of a new festival. Strong anchor for a music-focused Tokyo trip, though not by itself a reason to cross the Pacific.

es.why_it_matters: Cruza el umbral S porque no es simplemente una muestra de festival: es el prólogo público, de una sola noche, de una nueva institución jazzística de Tokio, curado por Hiromi y con una concentración deliberadamente intergeneracional de músicos que representan la escena japonesa contemporánea. Ishiwaka, Inoue, Baba, Matsui, Umei y compañía le dan una identidad instrumental e improvisatoria muy fuerte, mientras que el marco DAY 0 la convierte en una señal cultural de hacia dónde quiere ir el jazz de Tokio.
es.trip_verdict: S dentro de Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Vale proteger la noche y cruzar Tokio por esto; tiene un valor especial como fotografía concentrada del jazz japonés actual y como inicio ceremonial de un nuevo festival. Es una ancla fuerte para un viaje musical a Tokio, aunque por sí sola no justifica cruzar el Pacífico.
